Republicans Reject Democrats’ CLARITY Act Counteroffer as 60-Vote Outcome Remains Uncertain According to Punchbowl News and Crypto In America, Senate Republicans rejected Democrats’ latest CLARITY Act counterproposal ahead of Tuesday’s 2:15 p.m. ET cloture vote, which requires 60 votes to advance. Democrats sought tighter ethics rules, narrower BRCA developer protections and stronger conflict-of-interest provisions, while leaving stablecoin yield largely unchanged. Republicans say their latest text already includes 126 substantive Democratic changes and call it their “last, best and final offer.” The vote count remains uncertain. — link

CoinShares: AI Compute Generates About 3x More Profit per MW Than Bitcoin Mining CoinShares estimates that AI compute generates about $1.5 million in annualized profit per MW for Bitcoin miners, roughly three times the $0.5 million per MW generated by traditional mining, helping drive listed miners to redirect power and data center capacity toward AI and HPC. Companies with contracted AI or HPC capacity trade at an average 12.9x EV/NTM sales, compared with 3.7x for continuing miners without contracts. More than 4 GW of capacity has been contracted across the companies covered, but only about 550 MW is currently billing, leaving future valuations dependent on how quickly contracted capacity converts into revenue. — link

Crude Oil Tops $106, Hits Four-Month High According to Trading Economics market data, crude oil prices rose above $106 per barrel on September 15, 2026, U.S. Eastern Time, reaching a four-month high. The move was driven by tighter Middle East supply, with Saudi Arabia shutting the East-West pipeline, affecting the transport of 7 million barrels of crude per day, while protests also halted operations at several Libyan oil fields. In addition, China drew down oil inventories and increased orders in August. — link

U.S. Senate Fails to Advance CLARITY Act as Cloture Vote Falls Short of 60-Vote Threshold Just In: The U.S. Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633) after falling short of the 60 votes needed to invoke cloture. The measure received just 49 votes in favor, crypto journalist Eleanor Terrett reported. — link
